title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1967-01-27

ai_review.summary: Muddy audience cassette capture of an early‑67 Dead show, but the performance shines with a ferocious Viola Lee Blues, blistering Alligator and soaring New Potato Caboose.
ai_review.review: The tape is a low‑fidelity, hand‑held mono audience recording that many find almost unlistenable, yet it preserves a historic 1967 set where the band erupts in raw energy.  Highlights repeatedly mentioned are the volcanic Viola Lee Blues, the monster Alligator > Caution stretch and a powerful New Potato Caboose, with Pigpen’s organ and Jerry Garcia’s fiery guitar leading the charge.

ai_rating.rationale: Over thirty reviews provide a clear consensus: the musical performance is praised (high‑energy jams, standout songs) while the recording quality is widely criticized as poor.  The combined weighting yields an overall mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hand‑held mono cassette tape; very muddy, low‑fidelity and often described as unlistenable, though a few listeners say it becomes tolerable after the ears adjust.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑67 set with long improvisational stretches; the band moves from tight, high‑energy jams into extended psychedelic explorations, typical of the pre‑Wall of Sound era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note his fiery, overdriven guitar tone and soaring solos on Viola Lee Blues and Morning Dew.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is repeatedly praised as a dominant, swirling force throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Kreutzmann’s drumming is cited as low in the mix by one reviewer; later comments mention a two‑drummer setup on the Alligator > Caution segment.
